reason: REFUTED ON THE YEAR, NOT ON THE WORDS. The English is Hamburger's; the edition named is not the one anybody can show the words in. What holds up: the wording "But where danger threatens / That which saves from it also grows." is Michael Hamburger's rendering of "Wo aber Gefahr ist, wachst / Das Rettende auch", it sits in the opening quatrain after "Near is / And difficult to grasp, the God.", so lines 3 and 4 is the right locator, the sentence does end there in Holderlin (the next sentence starts "Im Finstern wohnen / Die Adler"), and it is not a competing translator's text: the three renderings set side by side on the markforshee page show how far apart the others are ("But where danger is, / Deliverance also beckons"; "But where there is danger, / A rescuing element grows as well"), so this English belongs to Hamburger and to nobody else. What breaks: the source line says 1966, and no source I could reach puts these words in the 1966 book. The only edition-anchored citation of this exact wording that I found is a scholarly one, in the apparatus to Jung's Black Books (Vol. VI, p. 255, fn 258), and it cites Friedrich Holderlin: Poems and Fragments, trans. Michael Hamburger (London: Anvil Press Poetry, 2004), p. 567. Every other witness (the Poem of the Week posting, the Jung-site posting) gives the wording and the translator's name with NO edition and NO year at all. That matters more than usual here because Hamburger did not translate Holderlin once: the accounts of his work list refinements and extensions across 1961, 1966, 1980 (Cambridge), 1986, 1994, 1998 and the 2004 Anvil fourth bilingual edition, the last described as carrying revisions and new translations. A line whose words are only provably in the 2004 text cannot ship claiming 1966. That is exactly the translation drift the track names as its main failure mode, and the rule is explicit: a translated line names the year of the published translation WHOSE WORDING IT USES. I tried to settle it in the 1966 volume and could not: archive.org holds the University of Michigan Press 1966 printing as friedrichholderl0000mich (656 images, creator Michael Hamburger, publisher The University of Michigan Press, date 1966, which does at least confirm the verifier's imprint), but the item is access-restricted and both search-inside endpoints returned empty; HathiTrust full-text search refused with a 403; the Google Books API is out of daily quota. So the 1966 wording is unknown to me, not disproved, and under this track's standard unknown loses. THE FIX IS SMALL AND THE LINE SHOULD SURVIVE IT. Cite the edition the words are demonstrably in. Everything else passes: shipped.js returns shipped [], near [], Holderlin at 0 for the year, cap 3, not banned, and he is the only Holderlin in the month's 54 candidates; scope is clean (a hymn drafted 1802 and published 1808, not scripture even though its subject is, and the two lines quoted carry no religious content at all); publishable; the source is 95 characters, leads with the name, has no dash and no straight double quote; the tag Poetry is the form of the work; and the theme fit is the best in this batch. SECOND, SMALLER REMARK: the evidence field concedes that no copy of the book was opened and that the archive.org record is a CATALOGUE record, which proves the volume exists and not that the line is in it. If the editor prefers 1966 to 2004 for any reason, then this must ship as a HEDGE whose note says plainly that the translator is certain, the edition is not.
